en: Related to the term artificial intelligence
is the term machine learning. And you can
really think of machine learning as a
subfield of AI
in which models learn useful parameters,
which is yet another term we'll dive in
later, or patterns from data rather than
having every decision rule manually
programmed. And therefore, machine learning
is the primary way of building modern
artificial intelligence systems because the
idea is that we don't don't build artificial
intelligence by simply giving the computer a
lot of predefined conditions and checks,
but to instead train a system that's
flexible and that can evolve and grow over
time, where the person or the team that's
building the artificial intelligence does
not have to anticipate all potential
scenarios in advance.
And I'll give you an example. If you, for
example, think about computer games,
in there you may be fighting enemies
enemies, not human enemies, but enemies
controlled by the computer. And those
enemies typically
are powered by artificial intelligence
that's not built with machine learning, but
where instead they have a bunch of
predefined rules of what to do in certain
situations. Take cover, run away, and so on.
Now, for a computer game, that is quite
reasonable because there you have a
predefined set of things that can happen in
the end. It's in the end a
controlled space. It's not the real world
after all,
and having a real powerful
AI model in such a computer game would
just not work. It would be very likely
pretty expensive to train and develop. It
would also likely require quite beefy
hardware and therefore make your game less
usable by a majority of players.
So that would be an example where we don't
have machine learning. On the other hand,
all these large language models and all
these algorithm-powering AI models are
typically built with machine learning to
make them more flexible and to detect
patterns in data which is used for training
humans may not be able to anticipate in
advance.
